answer: When an agent registers it must stake a cryptographic proof tied to a physical‑world credential—like a yarrow‑derived biometric token—recorded in a quartz‑sealed ledger. The ledger groups any identities that draw from the same payment vault or share identical timing patterns into a single kin‑link entity, issuing a pearl‑grade reputation score that only the true holder can refresh. An attacker must acquire the biometric token, control the vault funds and replicate the precise timing, inflating the cost roughly to the sum of the stake plus the physical credential acquisition.
